issues: /api/super-admin/admins enrichment loop (resolve_company_names + count_documents + payments.find per admin) makes first paint of SA layout take 10-20 seconds on preview; SA layout shows only a spinner during that time. Consider projecting `companies` differently or batching the enrichment to keep first paint <3 s.

Trial banner + Upgrade Now button live under the Subscription tab (activeTab==='subscription'). The default active tab is Profile, so a trial user opening ProfileModal does not immediately see the CTA. Consider auto-selecting the Subscription tab for is_trial users, or duplicating the Upgrade Now button onto the Profile tab near the 'Plan: Trial' chip so it is one click away.

action_items: MINOR (design): Auto-focus the Subscription tab in ProfileModal for is_trial users (or hoist the Upgrade Now CTA to the Profile tab) so the trial banner + Upgrade button are visible without a tab switch.
MINOR (perf): Speed up /api/super-admin/admins first paint — the per-admin resolve_company_names + payments.find loop blocks SA layout ~10-20 s in the preview env.
critical_code_review_comments: billing.py _compute_amount clamps `net = max(1, new_total - credit)` — good, prevents Razorpay ₹0 rejection. But the returned breakdown['net'] then no longer equals new_total-credit; frontend should show old_total/credit/net separately (not net = new_total - credit) — currently only used server-side so OK.

billing.py verify_payment idempotency: _apply_billing_success guards `if order_row.get('status')=='captured': return` — good. Consider a MongoDB unique index on billing_orders.order_id (currently a plain field) to protect against concurrent /verify + /webhook.

billing.py super_convert_trial calls _apply_billing_success (which sends welcome mail synchronously). Preview RESEND is stale so the mail may error — best-effort try/except is in place, no impact on the convert flow.

seller_panel.py update_invoice_status: the `total_paid + 1 < inv_amt` fallback allows a mark-paid without create_payment when the customer has accumulated enough payments — this bypasses the explicit linkage design goal. Consider requiring link_payment_id or create_payment always, and using the accumulated-payments check only as an advisory when both are absent.

support_tickets.py _fire_webhook: uses httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=3.0) per event — good. But it iterates hooks serially inside a single AsyncClient; a slow hook still blocks the response by up to 3 s. Consider asyncio.gather over the hook list, or fire-and-forget via background task.

super_admin.py list_admins performs N+1 queries (resolve_company_names + count_documents + payments.find per admin) — measurable slowdown as tenants grow. Recommend a single aggregation pipeline or Redis-cached rows keyed on updated_at.
